AdapterRun.description: One adapter's contribution to a corpus: which adapter, and the range it read.

from.description:
The full hash of the range's base commit: the commit the previous release
was tagged on. Absent for a release line with no release yet, whose range
starts at its root.

to.description:
The full hash of the range's head commit: the newest commit the adapter
read.

Bump.description: The release impact of a change or of a release as a whole.

ChangeKind.description:
The category of an itemized change, which decides the section it renders in.

The variants correspond one-to-one with the conventional-commit types, spelled
out rather than abbreviated, so a parser reading conventional commits maps onto
them mechanically while a producer writing prose reads a vocabulary that needs
no decoding. Whether a change is breaking is
carried by `ChangelogEntry.breaking` rather than by a variant, matching
conventional commits' treatment of it as a marker rather than a type.

A project typically renders `FEATURE`, `FIX`, `PERFORMANCE` and `REVERT`, and
omits the rest from published notes.

ChangeSource.description: A reference to something that accounts for a change.

Changelog.description:
A release's changelog as structured data.

This is the contract between a producer that may vary between runs — a
language model, a command, a conventional-commit parser, or a person — and
the deterministic consumers that render it. Authoring may vary; rendering may
not. Every published artifact describing a release is rendered from one
instance, so no two artifacts can disagree.

`proposed_bump` carries the producer's conclusion about release impact. It is
a proposal, never an authority: the release tooling computes the bump
independently and halts when the two disagree. Where a maintainer names the
bump explicitly, the named bump governs and the proposal is advisory.

entries.description:
The itemized record of what changed, in the order it should be rendered.

Renderers group entries by `kind` and preserve this order within each
group, so authoring order is presentation order.

A breaking change is an entry with `breaking` set, carrying its own
`migration`. There is no separate collection for them: a release-level
breaking note is an entry whose sources span the changes that caused it.

proposed_bump.description:
The release impact the producer concluded from the content.

Absent on a corpus the tooling assembled, which proposes nothing, and
required of every corpus a producer returns. Compared against the bump
the tooling computes. A disagreement halts the release for human
confirmation; it is never resolved by preferring one side.

schema_version.description:
Version of this schema that the instance conforms to.

Consumers reject an instance declaring a schema version they do not
implement rather than rendering it partially.

sources.description:
Every adapter that contributed material to this corpus, and the commit
range each read.

Written when the corpus is assembled and carried through authoring
unchanged, so a reviewer can tell what the prose was written from. Empty
for a corpus nobody assembled, such as one written by hand.

summary.description:
One or two paragraphs introducing the release in prose.

This is where a release earns readable notes: what changed in aggregate,
who should care, and what to do about it. Entries carry the itemized
record; this carries the narrative.

title.description:
A short headline for the release, at most one sentence.

Rendered above the entries where a target supports it. Omitted for
releases that carry no theme worth naming — most patch releases.

version.description:
The resolved version this changelog describes, without a tag prefix — for
example `1.4.0`.

Left unset while a changelog is being authored, and filled in once the
version is resolved. Renderers require it, because a rendered section is
headed by the version it describes.

breaking.description: Whether a consumer that upgrades is broken by this change.

derived.description:
Whether `summary` was derived mechanically from a commit subject rather
than written by a person or a producer.

Set when the tooling assembles an entry from a commit that carried no
author-written release-notes block. A producer that replaces the summary
with prose of its own clears it; one that keeps the derived summary
leaves it set, so a reviewer can see which lines nobody wrote.

detail.description:
Additional prose for a change that cannot be understood from its summary
alone.

Rendered beneath the summary. Most entries need none.

kind.description: What kind of change this is. Determines which section renders it.

migration.description:
What a consumer must do to adopt this change, where anything is required.

Required where `breaking` is set: a breaking change without migration
guidance is an incident report rather than a release note. Also used
where adoption is optional but non-obvious.

scope.description:
The part of the product this change affects, in the project's own
vocabulary — for example `transpilers/go` or `cli`.

The same notion as a conventional-commit scope. Rendered as a prefix
where a target supports it, and unset where a change is not scoped to one
area.

sources.description:
Where this change came from — the pull requests, commits and issues that
together account for it.

Rendered as links where the target supports it. An entry may cite several
sources of different kinds, which is how one entry describes work that
arrived across more than one pull request.

summary.description:
One line stating the change from the reader's point of view.

Written as an outcome a consumer can recognize, not as the work that
produced it: "closed decoders reject undeclared keys", not "refactored the
decoder".

CommitSource.description: A commit that carried a change.

hash.description: The full commit hash. Renderers abbreviate it for display.

IssueSource.description: An issue or work item a change resolves.

id.description:
The identifier in the tracker's own form — for example `strata-8da` or
`412`.

PullRequestSource.description: A pull request that carried a change.

number.description: The pull request number, as the hosting platform assigns it.
